questions.prompt: Who discovered penicillin, the first antibiotic, from a mould in 1928?
questions.explain: Fleming noticed that mould stopped bacteria growing on a plate.

questions.prompt: Why won't antibiotics cure a cold?
options: Colds are caused by viruses, and antibiotics only work against bacteria
questions.explain: Using antibiotics for viral infections also helps resistance spread.

questions.prompt: In the Petri Dish Lab, which disc produced the largest clear zone on the ordinary strain?
questions.explain: A bigger clear zone means more bacteria were stopped.

questions.prompt: On the resistant strain, the antibiotic disc had NO clear zone. What does this show?
options: These bacteria are not affected by that antibiotic
questions.explain: Resistant bacteria survive treatment and multiply.

questions.prompt: Which actions help prevent antibiotic resistance? Choose all that apply.
options: Take antibiotics only when prescribed by a doctor
Save leftover antibiotics for next time
Don’t ask for antibiotics for colds and flu
questions.explain: Misuse helps resistant bacteria survive and spread.

questions.prompt: How does a vaccine protect us?
options: It kills all germs in the body
It trains the immune system to recognise a pathogen, so the body can fight it quickly later
It makes us sweat out germs
questions.explain: Vaccines helped India become polio-free in 2014.

questions.prompt: In the handwashing test, unwashed hands gave 150 colonies and soap-washed hands gave 12. By what percentage did soap reduce the colonies?
In many places, antibiotics can be bought without a prescription. Should this be allowed? Give arguments on both sides and your conclusion.
questions.modelAnswer: For: people in remote areas far from doctors can get treatment quickly; it is cheaper and saves time. Against: people take antibiotics for viral infections or stop courses early, which speeds up antibiotic resistance, making common infections harder to treat for everyone; wrong doses can cause side effects. Conclusion: antibiotics should require a prescription, while governments improve access to doctors and telemedicine so people aren't left without care.
rubric: A valid argument against, linked to resistance
questions.explain: Criterion D: weigh individual and public health.
